1680: The safety card shows a very calm person doing very alarming things with excellent posture. Aspirational, honestly.
1681: You found your seat, then the person already in it, then a polite negotiation you quietly lost by one row.
1682: The tray table folds down just far enough to hold a cup and about half of your ambitions.
1683: Turbulence began, the whole cabin gasped, then it stopped and everyone pretended they hadn't.
1684: You read the entire safety card, twice, and now feel fully prepared for exactly nothing.
1685: The person beside you fell asleep on your shoulder. You now have a stranger and a responsibility.
1686: You planned the whole case in your head at altitude. Half of it made sense. That half will do.
1687: The window gave you six hours of sky and one very honest reflection of your own extremely tired face.
1688: You reclined your seat two whole centimeters and briefly felt like the most powerful person aboard.
1689: Somewhere over the middle of everything, the seat ahead reclined gently into your knees to say hello.
1690: The snack cart arrived, you chose very carefully, and received something small and mysteriously square.
1691: You dozed off mid-thought and woke up mid-drool, which is a different kind of progress, technically.
1692: The seatbelt sign switched on for no visible reason, and everyone obeyed it like a small law.
1693: You watched the little map on the screen inch along and felt personally responsible for the progress.
1694: The seat pocket held a card, a bag, and one mystery crumb from a braver traveler who came before.
1695: You settled in for the long flight with a snack and a firm intention to relax that lasted nine minutes.
1696: The small child two rows up narrated the whole flight. Best updates you got all day, honestly.
1697: You tried to sleep sitting perfectly upright, like a very tired statue with a case to solve.
1698: The pilot's voice came on, warm and calm, listing numbers you nodded at without understanding one.
1699: You raised the window shade to check on the sky, found it exactly where you left it, and felt reassured.
1700: Boarding began, so you joined the line early, then stood in it long enough to deeply regret joining early.
1701: You buckled the belt, tugged it snug, and briefly felt like you had accomplished a genuine task.
1702: The flight was long enough to read the menu four times and develop firm opinions about all of it.
1703: Your ears popped, the world got clearer, and your thoughts arrived a full moment after you did.
1704: You accepted a small cup of water and held it carefully, as if it were the last water on earth.
1705: The overhead bin closed with the calm confidence of a door that will not reopen easily later.
1706: The screen said three hours remained, then eleven minutes later said three hours remained. Bold of it.
1707: Everyone lowered their tray tables at once, like a very quiet, very well-organized little ceremony.
1708: You woke from a nap absolutely sure you'd solved it. You had not. It felt wonderful for one second.
1709: The engines hummed one long note for hours, and eventually you simply agreed to like it.
1710: You clutched your boarding pass the entire flight, in case anyone demanded proof you belonged up there.
1711: The cabin lights dimmed and the whole plane silently agreed to pretend it was the middle of the night.
1712: You looked out the window at nothing, then more nothing, then a bit of nothing with a cloud in it.
1713: You practiced looking wide awake for the landing, in case the new place was watching. It wasn't.
1714: The person across the aisle organized their bag three times. You admired the commitment quietly.
1715: You wrote your best idea on a scrap of paper up there and can no longer read a single word of it.
1716: The flight offered a movie, a nap, or serious thought about the case. You bravely chose all three, badly.
1717: You held very still through the turbulence, as if being calm might personally steady the whole plane.
1718: The hours passed the way hours do up here: slowly, then all at once, then very slowly again.
1719: You braced for the landing with everything you had, and when it came gently, you felt a little insulted.
